memoryTip: E-nerve-ate: strip the nerve/energy out — weaken (not energize!).
correctPassage: Heat and humidity can enervate even seasoned hikers.
wrongPassages: A cold shower and strong coffee will enervate you for the morning run.
The coach’s speech was meant to enervate the team into a furious comeback.
They hoped the rest day would enervate sore muscles back to full strength.

memoryTip: Belli- (war) + gerent — warlike and ready to fight.
correctPassage: A belligerent tone in the letter made negotiation unlikely.
wrongPassages: His belligerent handshake and warm smile put every guest at ease.
The mediator stayed belligerent by refusing to raise her voice or take sides.
They praised the belligerent cease-fire that ended every dispute without a threat.

definition: wanting or devouring great quantities of something
memoryTip: Vora = devour — a huge appetite for food, books, or work.
correctPassage: A voracious reader, she finished several novels each week.
wrongPassages: His voracious appetite was satisfied by half a cracker and a sip of water.
The voracious archive held only one short pamphlet no one ever opened.
She was a voracious student who never finished a single assigned chapter.

definition: a change of circumstances, often unwelcome
memoryTip: Vici-change: the ups and downs fortune throws at you.
correctPassage: The firm survived every vicissitude of the market cycle.
wrongPassages: Life under the monarchy was one long vicissitude of perfect, unchanging calm.
They planned for vicissitude by freezing every policy for the next decade.
The lake’s vicissitude meant the waterline never rose or fell by an inch.

definition: looking or sounding sad and dismal
memoryTip: Lugubrious funeral face — exaggeratedly mournful and gloomy.
correctPassage: A lugubrious soundtrack made the short film feel longer than it was.
wrongPassages: His lugubrious welcome was a bright grin and a round of cheerful jokes.
The parade stayed lugubrious with confetti, brass bands, and dancing crowds.
She delivered a lugubrious toast that left the room laughing for minutes.
